question: What Do the Catalog Visibility Options Actually Control?
metaDescription: Shop and search results, Shop only, Search results only, and Hidden each control a distinct combination of where a product can be found or purchased.
shortAnswer: Catalog visibility (set per product under Publish settings) controls where a product appears in browsing and search, independent of whether it can still be purchased directly by URL: "Shop and search results" (the default, fully visible everywhere), "Shop only" (appears in category/shop listings but not internal search), "Search results only" (findable via search but not browsable listings), and "Hidden" (excluded from both, but still directly accessible and purchasable if a customer has the direct link).

bodyHtml:
The Four Options Explained

These settings control discoverability, not purchasability — even a "Hidden" product remains a fully functional, purchasable product at its own direct URL, it just won't be found through normal browsing or search. This distinction matters for use cases like a product only meant to be linked directly (from an email campaign, a specific landing page) without appearing in general catalog browsing.

Common Use Cases for Each

  • "Shop and search results" is the correct default for the vast majority of products meant to be normally discoverable.
  • "Search results only" suits a product you don't want featured in general category browsing but should still surface if a customer searches for it specifically by name.
  • "Shop only" is less commonly used but could suit a product meant to be browsable in its category context without being a top search result for unrelated queries.
  • "Hidden" fits a product only meant to be accessed via a direct link — an exclusive offer, a product still being finalized but needing a working purchase link for internal testing, or a legacy product kept purchasable for existing customers with the link but not promoted generally.

Using These Settings Correctly

  1. Default to "Shop and search results" unless there's a specific reason to restrict discoverability.
  2. Use "Hidden" deliberately for direct-link-only products, understanding it doesn't prevent purchase, only browsing/search discovery.
  3. Review visibility settings periodically if products seem to be missing from expected listings, since this is a common, easily overlooked cause covered in more detail elsewhere.
